turns.content: In Bridges' exceptional Drosophila progeny, abnormal X-chromosome constitutions co-occurred with exceptional white-eye inheritance. What relationship is established by that observation alone?
Does this preliminary co-occurrence by itself identify a causal direction between chromosome constitution and eye color? Explain the evidential limit.
Compare two historical evidence streams: an ordinary sex-linked progeny ratio and Bridges' exceptional progeny whose predicted abnormal X constitutions were checked cytologically.
What criterion distinguishes direct chromosome-trait co-segregation evidence from an ordinary Mendelian ratio?
In Bridges' experiment, the two maternal homologous X chromosomes moved to the same pole during meiosis I. Classify this segregation event.
Derive the abnormal egg classes produced by this X-chromosome nondisjunction.
Explain how those eggs generate exceptional offspring and how the observed eye phenotypes matched the abnormal X-chromosome constitutions.
Identify the experiment that supplied the decisive evidence for the chromosomal theory and explain why the ordinary sex-linked ratio was less direct.
Check the chromosome terminology: distinguish homologous X chromosomes in meiosis I from sister chromatids.
State the historical conclusion with an appropriate qualification for the terminology and evidence available.
Give a concise final description of Bridges' experiment and how its cytology tracked exceptional white-eye inheritance.
